literal: Later he was transferred to Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He was later made Minister of Works.

literal: Yue's elder brother's son Lu had committed a crime; all the paternal uncles and brothers were executed, but Yue and his son were specially pardoned.
idiomatic: Yue's nephew Lu had offended; every uncle and brother was put to death, yet Yue and his son alone were spared.

literal: In the fourth year of Tianci an edict granted Yue an estate in the Southern Palace; Yue led household servants to develop it.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianci the court granted Yue a holding in the Southern Palace, and he set his household to work it.

literal: Surveillance officials reported that Yue's clothes were splendid and bright and that his bearing and deportment imitated a ruler's.
idiomatic: Inspectors reported that Yue dressed in bright finery and carried himself like a sovereign.

literal: When Taizu was unwell he was full of suspicion and had many men killed; Yue was executed.
idiomatic: Taizu, already ill and suspicious, had him killed.

literal: People of the time all considered it a wrongful death and mourned him.
idiomatic: All who heard of it called it a wrongful death and grieved.

literal: Yue was buried on the border of Shanyin west of Dai.
idiomatic: Yue was buried on the western border of Dai, at Shanyin.

literal: Later Emperor Shizu campaigned against the Helian; passing his tomb residence, he was moved to sorrow, issued an edict to build a temple, and ordered the people of one province to offer sacrifices in the four seasons.
idiomatic: Later, campaigning against the Helian, Emperor Shizu passed his tomb, was moved to sorrow, ordered a temple built, and commanded one province to sacrifice in the four seasons.

literal: He sought descendants of Yue fit to serve as generals and found his son Ling.
idiomatic: He sought a descendant of Yue fit for command and found his son Ling.

literal: He followed campaigns with merit and was permitted to inherit the rank.
idiomatic: Ling followed campaigns with merit and was allowed to inherit the title.

literal: Lu, at the beginning of Huangshi, followed the campaign against Murong Bao as Commandant of the City Gates.
idiomatic: Lu, at the opening of Huangshi, marched against Murong Bao as commandant of the city gates.

literal: He was transferred to Inspector of the Capital Region.
idiomatic: He was made inspector of the capital region.

literal: He was enfeoffed Duke of Gaoping and then executed.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Duke of Gaoping—and then executed.

literal: He Digan, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: He Digan was from Dai.

literal: His family was originally of a small clan; for generations they were honest and steady, and as generals they were famed for fairness.
idiomatic: His clan was small and for generations honest; as a commander he was famed for fairness.

literal: He was gradually promoted to Grand Chief of the Northern Tribes.
idiomatic: He rose to grand chief of the northern tribes.

literal: At the founding of Dengguo he was paired with Zhangsun Song; clear in hearing and judgment, he was loved and respected by men.
idiomatic: At the state's founding he was paired with Zhangsun Song—keen of ear and judgment, loved and respected.

literal: Taizu sent Digan to present a thousand horses and conclude a marriage with Yao Chang.
idiomatic: Taizu sent Digan with a thousand horses to seal marriage with Yao Chang.

literal: Chang died and Xing took the throne; he therefore detained Digan and broke the betrothal.
idiomatic: Chang died; Xing detained Digan and broke the match.

literal: Xing's younger brother Ping led troops to raid Pingyang; Taizu campaigned to pacify Ping and captured his generals Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and more than thirty others.
idiomatic: Xing's brother Ping raided Pingyang; Taizu defeated him and took Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and thirty more.

literal: [1] In Tianci, an edict that Marquis of Northern Xin An Tong escort Tang Xiaofang to Chang'an.
idiomatic: [1] In Tianci an edict ordered An Tong, Marquis of Northern Xin, to escort Tang Xiaofang to Chang'an.

literal: Later the Rouran She Lün allied with Xing in marriage and sent eight thousand horses.
idiomatic: Later the Rouran khan She Lün allied with Xing by marriage and sent eight thousand horses.

literal: Just as they were crossing the river, Helian Qubing resented Xing's friendship with our state and rebelled against Xing, intercepting She Lün's horses.
idiomatic: As they crossed the river, Helian Qubing, angered at Xing's friendship with us, rebelled and seized She Lün's horses.

literal: Xing then sent envoys, offering a thousand fine horses to ransom Bozhi and send Digan back.
idiomatic: Xing then sent envoys offering a thousand fine horses to ransom Bozhi and return Digan.

literal: Taizu wished to estrange the two enemies and therefore agreed.
idiomatic: Taizu meant to set the two foes against each other and agreed.

literal: While confined in Chang'an, Digan studied histories and mastered the Analects, Documents, and other classics; his bearing was elegant, like a Confucian's.
idiomatic: Confined in Chang'an he studied histories and the Analects and Documents; his bearing grew elegant, like a scholar's.

literal: When Taizu enfeoffed the meritous in general, though Digan was detained by Yao Xing, he was granted from afar the title Marquis of Xiangwu and added General of Qin Troops.
idiomatic: When merit was rewarded, though Xing still held him, Digan was enfeoffed from afar as Marquis of Xiangwu and General of Qin Troops.

literal: When Digan arrived, Taizu saw his speech and clothes resembled Qiang custom; he thought Digan had admired and learned them, grew angry, and killed him.
idiomatic: When Digan returned, Taizu saw his speech and dress in Qiang fashion, thought him a mimic, grew angry, and killed him.

literal: His younger brother Gui was also upright and refined.
idiomatic: His brother Gui was likewise upright and refined.

literal: He died together with Digan.
idiomatic: Gui died with him.

literal: Li Li, a man of Yanmen.
idiomatic: Li Li was from Yanmen.

literal: In Zhaocheng's time his father and grandfather entered the state.
idiomatic: In Zhaocheng's time his father and grandfather came north.

literal: In youth he was eloquent and quick, with ability and also military stratagem.
idiomatic: In youth he was quick and eloquent, gifted in arms as well as wit.

literal: At first he followed Taizu on his visit to the Helan tribe, among the twenty-one original followers.
idiomatic: At first he followed Taizu to the Helan, one of the twenty-one original followers.

literal: Taizu loved his artistry.
idiomatic: Taizu loved his skill.

literal: When the royal enterprise was still being founded, close aides were mostly kin; only Li was a lone man stationed far, not a relative by marriage — the age honored him for it.
idiomatic: While the realm was still being forged, confidants were kin; Li alone was a distant outsider, no in-law—men of the day held it an honor.

literal: He repeatedly had battle merit and was appointed Left Army General.
idiomatic: He won battle after battle and was named left army general.

literal: When Taizu campaigned against Murong Bao, Li commanded fifty thousand cavalry as vanguard; wherever the army went none failed to submit.
idiomatic: On Taizu's campaign against Murong Bao, Li led fifty thousand horse as vanguard; every place the host reached submitted.

literal: He was promoted to Left General.
idiomatic: He was raised to left general.

literal: When Murong Bao abandoned Zhongshan and fled east, Li pursued with light cavalry but did not overtake him and returned.
idiomatic: When Bao abandoned Zhongshan and fled east, Li rode light horse in pursuit, could not catch him, and turned back.

literal: Li was by nature blunt and arrogant, enjoying favor, not observing ritual; before Taizu he would stretch and act insolently without self-restraint, coughing and spitting as he pleased.
idiomatic: Li was blunt and arrogant, spoiled by favor, careless of ritual; before Taizu he lounged insolently, coughing and spitting at will.

literal: Taizu accumulated his old faults; in the third year of Tianxing he was executed.
idiomatic: Taizu tallied his old offenses; in the third year of Tianxing he was executed.

literal: Then authority grew stern; regulation of the host to observe humble courtesy began with Li.
idiomatic: From then on majesty was enforced and the court taught humble courtesy—beginning with Li.

literal: Liu Jie, a man of Xindu in Chang Le.
idiomatic: Liu Jie was from Xindu in Chang Le.

literal: His grandfather Sheng was skilled in divination.
idiomatic: His grandfather Sheng was versed in divination.

literal: In Zhaocheng's time the Murong clan came to present a woman; he became household retainer of the princess and followed into court.
idiomatic: In Zhaocheng's reign the Murong sent a princess; he became a household retainer and followed her into court.

literal: He was granted a wife and a son was born.
idiomatic: He was given a wife and had a son.

literal: His father Ti, in Taizu's time reached Administrator of Leling and was enfeoffed Baron of Xindu.
idiomatic: His father Ti, under Taizu, rose to administrator of Leling and was enfeoffed baron of Xindu.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: Ti died.

literal: Jie was by nature forceful and intelligent; he repeatedly followed campaigns with merit and was advanced to Duke of Kuaiji.
idiomatic: Jie was forceful and clever; he campaigned again and again with merit and was raised to Duke of Kuaiji.

literal: The Hexi Hu Zhang Wai, Jianxing King Shao, and others gathered factions in rebellion; Jie with Marquis of Yong'an Wei Qin led three thousand troops stationed at Xihe to pacify them.
idiomatic: Zhang Wai of the Hexi Hu, Jianxing King Shao, and others raised factions; Jie with Wei Qin, Marquis of Yong'an, took three thousand men to garrison Xihe and pacify them.

literal: He also with Qin and Meritorious General Yuan Qu attacked the rebellious Hu at Tujing.
idiomatic: He also joined Qin and Meritorious General Yuan Qu to strike the rebel Hu at Tujing.

literal: At the time Lishi Hu chief Chu Yijuan led Qubing's cavalry by way of Juan, cut off the mountain ridges to intercept Jie; Jie lost his horse, fought on the mountain with all his strength until arrows and blades were exhausted, was seized by the Hu and sent to Qubing.
idiomatic: Then Chu Yijuan of the Lishi Hu led Qubing's horse by Juan, blocked the passes, and cut Jie off; Jie lost his mount, fought on foot until steel was spent, was taken, and sent to Qubing.

literal: Jie's voice and spirit did not waver; he called Qubing by his style name and spoke with him, his expression calm.
idiomatic: Jie's voice never broke; he called Qubing by his style and spoke freely, his face unchanged.

literal: Qubing admired him and released him.
idiomatic: Qubing admired his spirit and let him go.

literal: Later he returned to the state and oversaw eastern affairs.
idiomatic: Later he returned and oversaw the eastern administration.

literal: When Taizong was ill, Shizu supervised the state; Jie with Gu Bi and others were selected to attend the Eastern Palace, handling critical affairs and presenting memorials on all departments.
idiomatic: When Taizong fell ill and Shizu oversaw the realm, Jie with Gu Bi and others were chosen to serve the Eastern Palace, handling secrets and reporting on every office.

literal: When Shizu took the throne, reporting on rebels and offering blunt advice — wherever he spoke it matched intent; they marveled at his pillar-and-timber usefulness and entrusted great responsibility.
idiomatic: At Shizu's accession he exposed rebels and spoke bluntly; his words always hit the mark, and the court, seeing a pillar of state, gave him heavy trust.

literal: When military and state affairs were discussed, court ministers all praised his ability.
idiomatic: In council on war and state, every minister praised his capacity.

literal: He was thereupon promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing and changed to Duke of Julu.
idiomatic: He was raised to director of the masters of writing and made Duke of Julu.

literal: When Shizu defeated the Rouran Dadan at Yunzhong, Jie said to Shizu: "Dadan relies on his numbers; though broken in spirit he flees north, I fear he does not dread past defeat and will come again to his death.
idiomatic: After Shizu broke the Rouran Dadan at Yunzhong, Jie told him, "Dadan still has his host; though routed north, he may not fear defeat and will return to die in battle.

literal: I beg that after the harvest is gathered we mount another great campaign, advancing east and west in two columns to attack him.
idiomatic: Gather the harvest, then strike again in force, east and west together."

literal: " Shizu approved his words.
idiomatic: Shizu agreed.

literal: Later in great deliberation on campaigns, Jie said Feng Bo should be pacified first; Shizu did not agree.
idiomatic: Later, debating campaigns, Jie urged pacifying Feng Bo first; Shizu refused.

literal: The Tiele new subjects complained that officers and clerks seized from them; all murmured in resentment, setting a date when cattle and horses had eaten their fill on the grass to flee north to the desert.
idiomatic: Tiele settlers complained that officers plundered them; murmurs spread, and they fixed a day—when the herds were fat on the grass—to flee north into the desert.

literal: Jie with Left Vice Minister An Yuan memorialized, wishing to move them west of the river before the ice broke up, so that when the ice melted they could not flee north.
idiomatic: Jie and An Yuan, left vice minister, urged moving them west of the river before the ice broke, so when it thawed they could not escape north.

literal: Shizu said: "That will not do.
idiomatic: Shizu said, "No.

literal: These people are long accustomed to wandering; they are like deer in a garden — pressed, they bolt; eased, they settle.
idiomatic: They have wandered for generations, like deer in an enclosure—drive them hard and they stampede; ease them and they stay.

literal: I myself have a way to handle them; there is no need to move them.
idiomatic: I know how to govern them; no need to relocate."

literal: " Jie and the others insisted, and he then permitted relocating more than thirty thousand households west of the river, as far as White Salt Marsh.
idiomatic: Jie pressed on, and the emperor allowed more than thirty thousand households to be moved west of the river, as far as White Salt Marsh.

literal: The new subjects were alarmed and all said, "Penning us in the midst of Hexi is to kill us," and wished to flee west to Liangzhou.
idiomatic: The settlers were terrified: "They have penned us in Hexi to slaughter us," and many meant to flee west to Liangzhou.

literal: Jie with Palace Attendant Gu Bi garrisoned north of the Yellow River at Wuyuan; An Yuan, Left Vice Minister, garrisoned north of Yueba city — to guard against them.
idiomatic: Jie with Gu Bi, palace attendant, held the north bank at Wuyuan; An Yuan held north of Yueba—to block them.

literal: Before long several thousand of the new subjects fled north on horseback; Jie pursued and attacked them.
idiomatic: Soon thousands fled north on horse; Jie pursued them.

literal: The fugitives ran out of provisions and died piled on one another.
idiomatic: The fugitives ran out of food and died in heaps.

literal: At that time the southern provinces suffered great floods and the people were blocked by famine.
idiomatic: That year the southern provinces flooded and the people starved.

literal: Jie memorialized, saying: "I have heard that Heaven and Earth are supremely fair, and therefore the ten thousand things all flourish;
idiomatic: Jie memorialized: "I have heard that Heaven and Earth are utterly fair, and so the ten thousand things thrive;

literal: the emperor is without private interest, and the black-haired people rely on him.
idiomatic: the emperor has no private aim, and the people lean on him.

literal: I bow to consider that Your Majesty, with divine martial bearing, has continued the line of restored brilliance, enlarged the great enterprise, and nourished the host of living beings.
idiomatic: Your Majesty, in divine martial splendor, has taken up the restored line, enlarged the great work, and nourished all life.

literal: Where your might has shaken, none has failed to submit; where your grace has reached, none however far has failed to cherish you — the governance of great peace is here.
idiomatic: Where your might has reached, none has refused submission; where your grace has spread, none however distant has failed to turn to you—great peace is at hand.

literal: In recent times border enemies have raided within; war-chariots have been driven again and again; Heaven has endowed sagely clarity, and wherever you have gone you have destroyed them.
idiomatic: Lately border foes have raided within and chariots have rolled out again and again; Heaven has given sagely clarity, and you have crushed them wherever you marched.

literal: Now that difficulty is settled, all have received reward; the high in merit have received ranks, the low in merit have received bounty — favor and gifts surpass the ancient norm.
idiomatic: Hardship ended, all have been rewarded—high merit ennobled, low merit gifted—bounty beyond the ancients.

literal: Yet the people of the commanderies and kingdoms, though they did not join the campaigns, have toiled at farming and sericulture to supply the army and state — truly the great root of ordering the age and the resource of the treasuries.
idiomatic: Yet commandery folk who never marched have tilled and mulberry-fed the host and treasury—the root of rule and the storehouse's grain.

literal: East of the mountains they have met with flood harm in particular; for years there has been no harvest, and they have gone elsewhere for food.
idiomatic: East of the mountains flood has ruined harvest after harvest, and they wander for food.

literal: I have heard that within the seas' bounds all are the king's subjects; they should receive added pity, covered and nourished like the wild goose's shade.
idiomatic: Within the seas all are your subjects; pity them and shelter them as the wild goose spreads its wings.

literal: Now the south has crushed a strong enemy and the west has defeated an ugly foe; within the four seas all is calm, men and spirits in harmony — if Your Majesty would share this fortune with the myriad people,
idiomatic: The south has broken a strong foe, the west a vile one; within the four seas all is calm, men and spirits at ease—if Your Majesty would share this fortune with the myriad people,

literal: then gracious feeling will harmonize the qi and the living will rejoice.
idiomatic: grace will harmonize the qi and the living will rejoice."

literal: " Shizu followed this and thereupon remitted one year's rent and tax throughout the realm.
idiomatic: Shizu agreed and remitted one year's rent and tax throughout the realm.

literal: Jie with Prince of Leping Pi directed the armies to take Shanggui.
idiomatic: Jie with Pi, Prince of Leping, led the armies to take Shanggui.

literal: When the army reached Qiyang, the people vied to present cattle and wine.
idiomatic: At Qiyang the people vied to offer cattle and wine.

literal: When Jie reached Shanggui, the generals all wished to execute the clan leaders to display royal might; Jie would not listen.
idiomatic: At Shanggui the generals wished to behead the clan chiefs to show royal might; Jie refused.

literal: He pacified Qin and Long; not a hair was harmed, and the people all secured their livelihoods.
idiomatic: He pacified Qin and Long without harm; every household kept its livelihood.

literal: Shizu was about to send the Longyou cavalry east to campaign against Goryeo.
idiomatic: Shizu meant to send the Longyou horse east against Goryeo.

literal: Jie advanced and said: "The new subjects of Long are just now touched by great transformation; they should be granted generous relief to fill them out.
idiomatic: Jie urged: "Long's new subjects have only just received your transformation; grant them ease and plenty.

literal: When horses and troops have full provisions, then they may be used.
idiomatic: When horse and arms are fed, then use them."

literal: " Shizu deeply accepted this.
idiomatic: Shizu took it deeply to heart.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned west, Jie was vanguard.
idiomatic: On the western campaign Jie led the van.

literal: Juqu Mujian's younger brother Donglai led more than ten thousand men to resist south of the city.
idiomatic: Juqu Mujian's brother Donglai brought more than ten thousand to resist south of the city.

literal: Jie trusted the diviner's words that the day and hour were inauspicious; he beat the drums and withdrew the formation, so the rear army did not advance and Donglai was able to enter the city.
idiomatic: Jie trusted a diviner that the day and hour were ill-omened; he beat the drums and drew the line back, the rear did not come up, and Donglai entered the city.

literal: Shizu was slightly displeased.
idiomatic: Shizu was somewhat displeased.

literal: Later Jie with Prince Jianning Chong directed the armies; from the San cheng Hu tribes they selected six thousand troops to garrison Guzang.
idiomatic: Later Jie with Chong, Prince Jianning, led the armies, chose six thousand from the San cheng Hu, and set them to garrison Guzang.
